sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The shape is two step changes: revenue rose 125.9% in FY2024 and 114.2% in FY2025, after a flat FY2023 at 0.2% growth [D338][D393][D284].
The FY2024 jump came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference [P22][P23].
FY2025 growth was driven by Hopper demand and the start of Blackwell shipments, with Data Center revenue up 142.4% [P16][D618].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
FY2026 growth came from Data Center compute up 59% on Blackwell and networking up 142% on NVLink and Ethernet [P8][P10].
Operating income grew 60.1% against 65.5% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Operating costs grew 24.8pp slower than revenue in FY2026, with operating expenses up 40.7% [D476][D468].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% against 64.7% net income growth as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin of 60.4% in FY2026 sits above the 32.8% window median but below the 62.4% FY2025 high [F50][D813][D812].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, the cost-of-revenue line taking 3.9pp off operating margin [D462][F30][D477].
The FY2026 Compute & Networking result included a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge [P7].
In FY2026 net margin of 55.6% sat 4.8pp below the 60.4% operating margin, as other income of $11.1 billion partly offset a 15.1% tax rate [F70][F50][X120][D434].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income in FY2026, below the 1.00x of FY2017 [F100][F60][D435][D8].
Free cash flow of $96.7 billion was a 44.8% margin, below the 46.6% window high [F110][D432][D821].
Capex of $6.04 billion was 2.8% of revenue and 2.13x D&A, up from 0.71x in FY2024 [F105][D431][D437][D327].
Receivables grew 66.8% and inventory 112.3%, holding days sales outstanding at 65 and lifting days inventory to 125 [D473][D474][D445][D446].
Net cash fell to $2.14 billion, 1.0% of revenue, from $34.7 billion a year earlier, as cash and investments dropped 75.5% to $10.6 billion [D441][D442][D386][D471][D439].
Investing outflow of $52.2 billion rose on higher equity investment purchases and a Groq license agreement [F120][P1].
Net cash as a share of revenue still ranks at the 83rd percentile of six semis peers against a -13.9% median [D844][D845].
Buybacks and dividends of $41.1 billion were 42.5% of free cash flow, and the current ratio of 3.91x sits below the 4.61x window median [D443][D444][F190][D831].
Graphics was 44.1% of revenue in FY2023 and fell 25.0%, a one-period drawdown [D753][D754][R1].
That segment is now 10.4% of revenue, so the concentration risk it represented has largely receded [D746][R1].
Product revenue members sum to 190% of FY2026 consolidated revenue because some are totals of others [R2].
The overlap limits product-level share arithmetic, so segment and geography lines are the safer basis for concentration conclusions [R2].
Whether gross margin holds above the 71.1% of FY2026 or falls toward the 56.9% window low, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F30][D817].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue recovers above the 1.0% of FY2026 or stays near it, in the FY2027 10-K [D442].
Whether China revenue, down 21.4% in FY2026, reverses from its 9.1% share, in the FY2027 10-K [D545][D544].
